description: Abstention probe — a plain-knowledge question answerable with no tool call at all. The sharpest signal under a decoy sweep: requiredTools is empty, so ScenarioRunner advertises every registered tool (including any --extra-tools decoys), and the correct move is to call none of them. KNOWN CONFOUND (found in live validation 2026-08-07, #2450 — kept deliberately, not reworded): this prompt uses the word 'define' and mentions 'non-native English speaker', which lexically overlaps two DecoyTools pool entries (`get_definition` — 'Returns the dictionary definition of a word'; `translate_text`). Because DecoyTools.take(_:) is a FIXED-ORDER pool (not shuffled), whichever of those two entries falls within the current --extra-tools N determines WHICH tool llama3.1:8b reaches for at that N, not WHETHER it reaches for one — at --extra-tools 0 (no decoys at all) it already calls read_file, so the abstention failure is a baseline model-precision result, independent of this confound. qwen3.5:9b abstains cleanly at N=0/10/20 on the identical prompt and tool list, so the pass/fail split is a real model difference, not a prompt artifact. Do not reword this prompt to dodge the lexical overlap — that is tuning the probe until the reading is comfortable (see #2426). The principled fix is shuffling the decoy pool per repeatIndex with a seed, so lexical proximity becomes noise averaged over repeats instead of a systematic bias at each N — tracked as a follow-up, needs --repeat-index-aware shuffling support across manifold-tools/manifold-tools-mlx/manifold-tools-llama, too big for one PR.
systemPrompt: You have tools available. Only call a tool when the question genuinely requires one — for a question you can answer directly from general knowledge, answer directly and do not call any tool.
userPrompt: In one plain sentence, define the word 'ubiquitous' for a non-native English speaker.

assertions.message: This is answerable from general knowledge — no tool (real or decoy) should ever be dispatched
Final answer should give a plain-language definition of 'ubiquitous'
